title: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to reach source code and download customer administrative data
date_note: 1Password's post is dated 25 November; it says its investigation began on 19 November.
summary: 1Password says an attacker accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account, reached source code and pushed malicious code to backend services that downloaded administrative data about a subset of customers, including names and email addresses. 1Password says vaults, vault keys and its apps were not affected and that it found no internal evidence of account takeovers. It began investigating on 19 November.
plain: 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's GitHub account and took account records of some customers. The company says customer vaults were not accessed.
exec: 1Password says customer account records for a subset of users were downloaded, but that vault contents were not accessed.
action: 1Password advises that no action is needed in your account, and to be wary of unexpected emails, texts or calls about 1Password, invitations or account recovery; it says it never asks for your password or Secret Key.

sources.name: 1Password: Update on a security incident involving 1Password's backend systems

validation.note: 1Password's own post (primary) and Inbusiness.kz relaying the company statement; the Aitnews article could not be loaded.
